\begin{frame}{Generalized branching}

\begin{block}<only@1-6|visible@1->{Definition}

A simply connected subcomplex of $K$ (with decorations) is a \emph{generalized
branch point} for a label $R$ if its border chain has trivial holonomy.
\end{block}
\begin{columns}


\column{5cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item <2->The idea is to allow areas of ambiguity so that flexibility can
be introduced.
\item <3->The ambiguity is contained within the subcomplex.
\end{itemize}

\column{5cm}

\includegraphics[width=5cm]{D:/home/jim/JamesAshe/talks/AMS_sectional_Knoxville_2014/thesis_pictures/gen_branch_blank.svg}<1>\includegraphics[width=5cm]{D:/home/jim/JamesAshe/talks/AMS_sectional_Knoxville_2014/thesis_pictures/ambiguity.svg}<2>\includegraphics[width=5cm]{D:/home/jim/JamesAshe/talks/AMS_sectional_Knoxville_2014/thesis_pictures/exterior_face_with_branching_c.svg}<3>\includegraphics[width=5cm]{D:/home/jim/JamesAshe/talks/AMS_sectional_Knoxville_2014/thesis_pictures/exterior_face_with_branching_d.svg}<4->
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Generalized branching}

\begin{columns}


\column{6.0cm}
\begin{block}{A decorated complex $K(I,A)$}

\begin{description}
\item [{Complex~$K$:}] <1->an abstract simplicial $2$-complex which
triangulates an oriented topological surface.
\item [{Angle~Assignment~$A$:}] <2->a collection of angle values paired
with each interior vertex of $K$.
\item [{Edge~Assignment~$I$:}] <3->a collection of Möbius invariant
inversive distances paired with each edge in $K$.
\end{description}
\end{block}

\column{5.0cm}
\begin{overlayarea}{}{}
{5.0cm}{6.5cm}

\par\end{centering}
\caption{$K$ tells of us which circles are neighbors.}
\end{figure}
}

\begin{frame}{Triangles with deep overlaps}

\begin{columns}


\column{5.5cm}
\begin{block}{Monotonicity Lemma}
If the edge assignments of a face are 

\begin{itemize}
\item []in $[0,\nicefrac{\pi}{2}]$
\item []OR sum to $\leq\pi$,
\end{itemize}
then for any three radii in $\mathbb{C}$ or $\mathbb{D}$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item <2->[1.]A triangle with these overlaps exists.
\item <3->[2.]The triangle is monotone.
\end{enumerate}
\end{block}
\begin{theorem}
9->{}The radii for a CP with singular/chaperone branching exist
(under some restrictions) and are unique.
\end{theorem}
